title: docs: name the epic-final designation (update_epic finalTaskId) in SCHEMA, CONFIGURATION and the breakdown, QA and regression skills
description:
Split out of task-cd2e447728224044abe7fa669d42f7fb. That task adds Epic.finalTaskId, set with moe.update_epic, and makes get_context isEpicFinal and delivery/policy.ts isEpicFinalTask follow it. An epic with no valid designation falls back to the highest `order` among its non-ARCHIVED tasks, ties counting. That task updates docs/MCP_SERVER.md and the moe-planning skill (its DoD) and stops at the daemon's 10-file plan limit, so these references still describe only the old highest-order rule:

- docs/SCHEMA.md: the Epic shape has no finalTaskId.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: the qualityGateScope row says "the epic's final task (highest `order` among siblings)".
- docs/skills/moe-epic-breakdown/SKILL.md: says to create the hardening task "at the highest `order`" and never says to designate it, so new epics stay undesignated and keep the drift.
- docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md (the mid-epic check) and docs/skills/regression-check/SKILL.md: say "moe.list_tasks {epicId} and compare order" instead of reading get_context task.isEpicFinal.

Regenerate packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/skillFiles.ts with `npm run generate-skill-files` in packages/moe-daemon. Do not use `npm run build` for this: its prebuild also regenerates initFiles.ts from docs/roles.
definitionOfDone: docs/SCHEMA.md's Epic shape lists `finalTaskId?: string` with the rule. The designated final task counts only while it names an existing, non-ARCHIVED task of the same epic; otherwise the highest-order fallback applies. docs/CONFIGURATION.md's qualityGateScope row names the designated final task instead of "highest `order` among siblings".

moe-epic-breakdown tells the architect to designate the integration-and-hardening task with moe.update_epic { epicId, finalTaskId } right after creating it, and to re-designate it if the epic later grows past that task.
moe-qa-loop and regression-check tell the agent to place a task by reading get_context task.isEpicFinal, not by comparing `order` via moe.list_tasks.

packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/skillFiles.ts is regenerated from docs/skills, and only the edited skills' entries change. A fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/util/skillFiles.test.ts` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
Three skills, mirroring the wording moe-planning already landed (git show HEAD:docs/skills/moe-planning/SKILL.md, lines 27 and 39).

(1) docs/skills/moe-epic-breakdown/SKILL.md, '## End the epic with an integration-and-hardening task': keep 'at the highest `order`', since order still ranks claims, and add two instructions.
- Designate the task with moe.update_epic { epicId, finalTaskId } right after moe.create_task returns its id. Reason: `order` is a per-column sort position that board drags and new rows rewrite, so it cannot name the final task on its own.
- Re-designate it with update_epic and the new id whenever the epic grows past that task: a new closing task replaces it, or work is re-sliced after it. Then get_context isEpicFinal and the quality gate follow the real closing task.

(2) docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md, '## Review depth follows the task's position in its epic': replace the parenthetical '(sibling tasks come after it — check `moe.list_tasks {epicId}` and compare `order`)' with a check on the task.isEpicFinal that moe.get_context returns (QA's default read includes it). false means mid-epic; true means the epic-final/hardening bar. At most one clause may say it follows the epic's designated finalTaskId, else the highest-order fallback, so a dragged or newly created row does not change it. Leave untouched the phrases qaCommitPolicy.test.ts pins in this file and its generated copy ('bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'land it yourself', 'record_commit'), and add neither phrase that test forbids.

(3) docs/skills/regression-check/SKILL.md:
- Replace 'Unsure of your position? `moe.list_tasks {epicId}` and compare `order`. No siblings after you → treat it as epic-final.' with: read moe.get_context task.isEpicFinal. true means epic-final (the full run); false means mid-epic. A task with no epic reads true.
- In the mid-epic bullet, '(there are sibling tasks after this one in the epic)' becomes '(get_context task.isEpicFinal is false)' or an equivalent.

No other text changes. Keep each frontmatter block intact, because the generator stamps its sha marker inside it. Use the CLI's file-editing tool and keep LF endings. The moe-planning skill and docs/MCP_SERVER.md belong to task-cd2e447728224044abe7fa669d42f7fb: do not touch them, and never hand-edit the .moe/skills mirror.

Regenerate packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/skillFiles.ts with the generator only. Never use npm run build: its prebuild also deletes dist and regenerates initFiles.ts from docs/roles. Never hand-edit the file.

On WSL the shared checkout's tsx and vitest are Windows builds, so work in a Linux snapshot (see mem:gotcha-linux-vitest-reuse-native-node-modules):
- SNAP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-ec99-gate.XXXXXX).
- git -C <repo root> archive HEAD | tar -x -C $SNAP. Archive the whole repo, because step 4's docs tests read root CLAUDE.md, .gitignore and docs/.
- Overlay exactly the five edited docs from the worktree and cmp each one.
- Symlink $SNAP/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules to /tmp/moe-linux-daemon.3EJTl5/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules, after checking that its package.json and package-lock.json equal the snapshot's modulo CR. If they differ or it is gone, run npm ci in the snapshot.
- Run (cd $SNAP/packages/moe-daemon && env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=<nvm node bin>:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin npm run generate-skill-files).

The architect verified on 2026-10-27 that HEAD's skillFiles.ts regenerates byte-identical from HEAD's docs/skills (65 files across 17 skills). So diff the output against git show HEAD:packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/skillFiles.ts: only the moe-epic-breakdown, moe-qa-loop and regression-check SKILL.md entries may change, meaning their text and their sha marker. Error handling: if any other entry changes (a peer edited another skill since), or the generator fails, stop and report it with the diff. Never trim or hand-merge the generated file. cp the result over the worktree file and cmp it. On native Windows, npm run generate-skill-files may run in place in packages/moe-daemon (the generator only, never build).

Verification gate, run once. Re-sync all six final files into $SNAP and cmp each one. From $SNAP, under the same env -i, run exactly: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/util/skillFiles.test.ts src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts src/util/executionContractDocs.test.ts src/util/daemonGitDocs.test.ts src/util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts. On native Windows, run it in place.

This is a superset of the DoD's skillFiles.test.ts:
- qaCommitPolicy pins the moe-qa-loop text in both the source and the generated copy, so a stale or damaged regeneration fails it;
- the three docs tests read SCHEMA.md and CONFIGURATION.md.

Freshness proof: run npm run generate-skill-files in $SNAP again and cmp its output with the worktree's skillFiles.ts. They must be identical.

Require exit 0 and zero failed tests. Submit { command, exitCode, outputTail } to complete_task, and name the tested root and its base commit in the summary. Error handling: on a failure, fix the docs input in the worktree, re-sync, regenerate and re-run the same command. Never edit the generated file by hand or weaken a test. Never install, build or run vitest in the shared checkout's packages/moe-daemon from WSL.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Keep it as one docs-sweep task with the generated file: 6 distinct files, past the 5-file warning but well under the 10-file limit, all mechanical. The 6th file forces the heavy tier, so the plan runs on Opus at the xhigh floor. Splitting off the regeneration would leave skillFiles.ts stale between landings, and qaCommitPolicy.test.ts asserts that the moe-qa-loop source and its generated copy agree, so a split breaks the suite in the middle. No npm run build: its prebuild cleans dist and regenerates initFiles.ts. No older-daemon fallback text in the skills: the plugins bundle a matching daemon, and the DoD says to stop comparing order. No edits to docs/MCP_SERVER.md or the moe-planning skill: task-cd2e4477 owns them.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- isEpicFinalTask (delivery/policy.ts:211) is the one rule:
  - no epic means final;
  - a valid designation (existing task, same epic, not ARCHIVED) makes only that task final;
  - otherwise own order >= the max order over non-ARCHIVED siblings (ties count).
- update_epic validation:
  - validateEpicUpdates: max 200, trimmed, '' clears (the key is dropped);
  - assertDesignatable refuses no-such-task, other-epic and ARCHIVED ids before any write.
- get_context serves task.isEpicFinal to QA by default. The QA trim omits only epicSiblings, planningNotes and routing (getContext.ts:35).
- The landed moe-planning wording is the house phrasing (HEAD lines 27 and 39).
- HEAD's generated skillFiles.ts regenerated byte-identical from HEAD docs/skills in a scratch Linux snapshot on 2026-10-27 (65 files across 17 skills).
- The generator reads docs/skills relative to packages/moe-daemon/scripts and LF-normalizes before hashing.
- qaCommitPolicy.test.ts pins sentinel phrases in moe-qa-loop (source and generated).
- executionContractDocs, daemonGitDocs and taskTimeBudgetDocs read SCHEMA.md and CONFIGURATION.md.
